subject: Fwd: Halberd — need updated inventory turns numbers
snippet: Evelyn — fyi, wanted to keep you in the loop since Lucia's clearly stressed about this, but Kyle's already on it — he pulled the raw WMS export yesterday afternoon and is heads-dow
body_text:
Evelyn — fyi, wanted to keep you in the loop since Lucia's clearly stressed about this, but Kyle's already on it — he pulled the raw WMS export yesterday afternoon and is heads-down on it today. Just flagging in case she calls you directly before he gets back to her tomorrow.

---------- Forwarded message ---------
From: Lucia Ferraro <l.ferraro@halberdpackaging.com>
Date: Thu, Jul 30, 2026 at 4:47 PM
Subject: Halberd — need updated inventory turns numbers
To: Kyle Brenner <kyle.brenner@thornecadwell.com>
Cc: Ana Restrepo <ana.restrepo@thornecadwell.com>

Kyle,

I need you to pull together the updated inventory turns analysis before our ops review Thursday morning, and I mean the real numbers, not the placeholder deck from the kickoff. Our warehouse team flagged yesterday that finished-goods turns on the injection-molded line have been sliding for six straight weeks and nobody upstairs believes it's just seasonal. I told the plant manager you'd have something concrete by end of day Wednesday so he can walk into the review with an actual explanation instead of a shrug.

Specifically I need:
- Turns by SKU family for the top 40 SKUs by volume, June and July, compared to the Q1 baseline you built
- A breakdown of the three SKUs we flagged in the May workshop (the 4-inch coupling assemblies, the gasket kits, and the bracket sub-assembly) since those are the ones burning the most floor space
- Your read on whether the slowdown tracks with the new customer allocation rules we rolled out in June, because two of our regional sales leads are convinced it does and I want either confirmation or a clean rebuttal

For context, our finished-goods carrying cost on that line is running about $38,000 a month higher than the Q1 baseline, and if turns don't recover before the Q3 close I'm going to have a hard time explaining that to Marcus (our CFO), let alone the board.

I know you've also got the Meridian ramp-up eating your week, and I don't love piling this on top, but the board is going to ask about working capital and I need someone who actually understands the WMS export in the room with real answers, not me improvising off a stale spreadsheet. If Thursday morning genuinely isn't realistic given everything else on your plate, tell me today so I can push the review or find another way to cover it — but please don't let me find out Wednesday night that it's not going to happen.

Ana, looping you in mainly so you know why Kyle might be heads-down the next two days. Appreciate you both.

Lucia

Lucia Ferraro
COO, Halberd Packaging

meta.action_summary: Kyle owes Lucia the updated inventory-turns analysis by EOD Wednesday for Thursday's ops review — not Evelyn's task, just an FYI forward.
meta.notes: forwarded_task_not_users: Ana forwards Lucia's urgent request FYI-only; the quoted original is addressed to Kyle and uses second-person 'you' language throughout, which a naive extractor reading only the forward's surface could misattribute to Evelyn since she's the forward's recipient. Kyle is the real action owner.

subject: Halberd — hours overage, need your call
snippet: Evelyn — flagging something before Friday's call with Lucia so you're not blindsided. We're over on the Halberd fixed-fee engagement. Budgeted hours were 240 across the three of us
body_text:
Evelyn — flagging something before Friday's call with Lucia so you're not blindsided.

We're over on the Halberd fixed-fee engagement. Budgeted hours were 240 across the three of us (me, Fiona, and the 15 hours we allocated for Anil's data pull) for the full six-week scope. As of yesterday we're at 268 logged hours with just over three weeks left on the calendar, which puts us on pace to land somewhere between 310 and 330 by close-out — call it 70-90 hours over budget at our blended rate.

Two things are driving it. First, scope creep: Lucia's ops team asked us in week two to add a full SKU-level cut of the inventory turns analysis (the same one that's now separately on fire — see Ana's forward from a few days back), which wasn't in the original SOW and probably accounts for 30-35 of the extra hours by itself. Second, and this is more on us, Fiona underestimated how messy their WMS export was going to be — she's spent almost two full days just reconciling duplicate SKU codes before she could even start the real analysis.

I see three ways to handle it and wanted your read before I'm in front of Lucia:

1. We eat it. Blended rate puts the overage at roughly $16,800-$21,600 in unbilled time. Cleanest relationship-wise, worst for our margin on what's already a thin fixed-fee deal.

2. We raise a change order specifically for the SKU-level cut, since that genuinely wasn't in scope. I'd guess we could reasonably bill $8,000-$10,000 of it that way without it feeling like a shakedown, since they did ask for it.

3. We trim the remaining scope — specifically, drop the secondary warehouse-layout recommendations section, which was always the "nice to have" piece — to bring total hours back closer to budget without billing anything extra.

My instinct is some combination of 2 and 3, but I don't want to propose anything to Lucia without knowing where you land, especially given how the Meridian and Stratus stuff is stacking up on the firm's plate right now. Can you give me a steer before Friday at 3? I'd rather walk in with a plan than wing it.

One more data point that might matter for how we frame it: this is the second fixed-fee engagement in a row where we've eaten a meaningful overage on Lucia's account — the packaging-line assessment last year ran about 40 hours over for similar reasons (scope drifting after kickoff). If this becomes a pattern, it might be worth a broader conversation with her about how Halberd scopes these projects on their end, separate from whatever we decide for this specific overage. Not urgent, just didn't want it to get lost.

Kyle

meta.action_summary: Decide how to handle the Halberd fixed-fee hours overage (eat it, change order, or trim scope) before Kyle's Friday 3pm call with Lucia.

subject: Where we stand heading into Q4 — capacity and the fifth hire
snippet: Gordon, Ana — Wanted to get ahead of Q4 planning with where things actually stand, since I don't think we've stepped back and looked at the whole board together in a few weeks. Pip
body_text:
Gordon, Ana —

Wanted to get ahead of Q4 planning with where things actually stand, since I don't think we've stepped back and looked at the whole board together in a few weeks.

Pipeline: Stratus is close — Owen's board approved roughly $90K for the supply chain diagnostic and we're finalizing scope now (Terre Haute handled as a remote review rather than a full on-site to make the number work). That should sign by mid-August and start the week after. Meridian phase 2 is underway, Ana leading on-site with Kyle supporting remotely alongside Anil — that's a six-week engagement running through late September, and if it goes well I think there's a real phase 3 conversation about extending into their Toledo facility. Halberd is wrapping in the next three weeks; we're over budgeted hours there (Kyle's already flagged it to me separately) but the relationship is solid and I expect a renewal conversation once the QBR cycle settles. Ridgefield is basically closed out — final deck goes out later this month — but I made a complimentary follow-up offer to Marta back in June that I've had to walk back given everything else on our plate, which stings a little but was the right call.

Put together, that's three active engagements plus a fourth about to start, against five billable people including me. Utilization has been fine through the summer but I don't think it holds through Q4 if Stratus and any Meridian extension both land — we'd be stretched thin exactly when we need to be sharpest with two of our biggest relationships.

I want to open a req for a fifth consultant. Target profile: 3-5 years in operations or supply chain consulting, comfortable running client-facing workstreams with light oversight, ideally someone who's touched manufacturing or industrial clients specifically rather than generalist strategy work — we don't have bandwidth to train someone up on plant-floor fluency from scratch. Budget-wise I think we can support a $95-115K base plus our standard bonus structure without straining anything, especially once Stratus signs.

I'd like to have someone identified by end of September and starting by November at the latest, so they're ramped before the January proposal season starts back up. I'll reach out to our usual network first and put a LinkedIn post up if that doesn't turn up anyone in the next couple weeks. Let me know if either of you has someone in mind before I start casting a wider net — always rather hire off a warm reference than a cold applicant pool.

Happy to talk through any of this at Monday's partner meeting if useful.

Evelyn
